title: Keep the newest reading of each sensor

blocks.text: The greenhouse dashboard reads its sensors from a message queue in batches. Since the queue started delivering more than one reading per sensor in a batch, the dashboard page fails to load; and since a new sensor was installed without calibration, it fails for every batch that contains that sensor. When it does load, the operators sometimes see a vent at an angle it left minutes ago.
`Readings.dashboard(...)` already formats the page. Finish the two `TODO`s in `src/main/java/practice/Readings.java`:

items: `latestBySensor(...)`: one entry per sensor, the reading that was taken last;
`unitBySensor(...)`: one entry per sensor that has a unit; an uncalibrated sensor has none.

blocks.text: A batch can hold any number of readings of a sensor, in any order. About six lines in total.

cases.says: with one reading per sensor, each sensor maps to that reading and its unit, and the dashboard shows them
a sensor that reports several times in a batch gets one entry, not an exception
the reading kept is the one taken last, not the one that arrived last
a sensor with no unit is left out of the unit map instead of failing the batch

origin.section: Collectors.toMap Throws on a Duplicate Key or a null Value Until You Say What to Do

concepts: A merge function that keeps the value seen last is wrong when input arrives out of order; BinaryOperator.maxBy with a Comparator keeps the one the data says is newest.
Collectors.toMap throws IllegalStateException on a duplicate key unless given a merge function, and NullPointerException on a null value even with one, so nulls are handled before the collector.
